jobs.title: Call for Applicants: Advisory Committee – Project on Criminalisation of Environmental Human Rights Defenders
jobs.reason: This is a call for established experts to sit on an advisory committee, not a paid entry-level role — it seeks activists and specialists with regional experience in East Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia, and is effectively a volunteer/advisory posting rather than a genuine paid vacancy for the candidate. The human-rights and securitisation topic is of real interest, but the level and nature of the position are a hard mismatch.

jobs.title: Auditor Integrated Systems and AS9100
jobs.reason: Requires at least 5 years of relevant industry experience plus a recognised auditor qualification/accreditation for AS9100, both essential requirements the candidate plainly lacks. The role is a technical quality-management auditing position wholly outside the candidate's research and policy background and interests.

jobs.title: Assessment Client Operations Team Lead
jobs.reason: A "Team Lead" role requiring proven cross-regional team management, succession planning and performance management — well beyond entry-level and far past what RA/student-assistant work supports. The certification-operations subject also sits outside all three interest zones.

jobs.title: Performance & Capability Consultant FTC
jobs.reason: Not entry-level — this is a senior consultant role (Band E, £80k+) requiring a proven track record of delivering organisational development and leadership outcomes, experience coaching senior stakeholders, and SAP/Centre of Expertise experience the candidate does not have. It is also an HR/organisational-development function well outside the candidate's research and policy interest zones.

jobs.title: Director of FP&A
jobs.reason: A Director-level finance role requiring significant FP&A leadership experience and a professional accounting qualification (ACA/ACCA/CIMA) — none of which the candidate holds. It is far above entry-level, in a wholly unrelated finance domain, and fails multiple hard disqualifiers.

jobs.title: Call for Applicants: Advisory Committee — Project on Criminalisation of Environmental Human Rights Defenders
jobs.reason: This is a call for "experts" to join an advisory committee — it seeks established specialists with recognised expertise, not an entry-level paid role, and it is an unpaid/advisory position rather than a genuine salaried vacancy. Although the human-rights and securitisation subject matter is genuinely in the candidate's interest zone, the seniority/expert requirement and non-paid advisory nature disqualify it.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Editor
jobs.reason: The role requires an essential life-science degree (preferably pharmacy/pharmacology) plus clinical or medical-writing experience, and preferably a PhD — qualifications the candidate, whose background is IR and international law, plainly lacks. The subject matter (pharmaceutical/clinical publishing) also sits entirely outside the candidate's interest zones.

jobs.title: Security Consultant - Governance Risk and Compliance
jobs.reason: This is a deep-technical cybersecurity GRC consulting role requiring practical experience delivering security engagements across IT/OT/ICS environments, working knowledge of networking, operating systems and cybersecurity technologies, plus stakeholder-facing client delivery — essentials the candidate's profile does not meet. It is also framed as an experienced consultant expected to lead full engagement lifecycles and mentor others, not an entry-level post. The subject sits well outside the candidate's international-law and policy focus.

jobs.title: Undergraduate Programme Administrator
jobs.reason: Eligible and entry-level-accessible — the essentials (Microsoft Office, accuracy, communication, degree level) are within reach and the candidate has HEI administrative experience from the German Rectors' Conference, though it lacks the LSE-specific systems (SITS, Moodle, Akari) and dedicated student-facing pastoral experience. It is a London-based higher-education administration role, which is only tangential to the candidate's core research and policy interests, so despite being a solid winnable application, the interest pull is low.
jobs.salary: £36,513–£41,565 pa inclusive, progressing to £44,468 pa inclusive

jobs.title: Intercompany controller
jobs.reason: This is a specialist finance / accounting role requiring intercompany reconciliations, journal postings and R2R accounting expertise the candidate does not have — a clear skills mismatch and outside all interest zones. It is neither a research/policy role nor within the candidate's competencies.

jobs.title: Quantitative Analyst - Model Development Team
jobs.reason: The essential requirements — a Master's in a quantitative discipline like Financial Engineering plus programming and model-development experience in VBA/Python/R for credit-risk and statistical modelling — are well beyond the candidate's analysis-level Python and non-quantitative IR background. This is a deep-technical quantitative-modelling role, not a fit, and it sits outside the candidate's interest zones.

jobs.title: Policy Fellow (Economic and Fiscal Policy)
jobs.reason: This is a senior "Fellow" role with salary and duties well above entry level — it requires leading projects, supervising Policy Analysts, and demonstrated experience working with government bodies and senior policymakers, none of which the candidate has. It also demands substantive fiscal/economic and climate-policy expertise plus advanced quantitative modelling (Stata/R/Python at data-analysis level for financial data) that fall outside the candidate's skill set and interests, and it sits outside all three interest zones.
jobs.salary: £53,949–£62,160 pa (progression to £69,073), inclusive of London allowance

jobs.title: Research Officer (NeST project)
jobs.reason: Essential requirements include a completed (or near-submission) PhD in statistics or a related subject, a solid background in mathematical statistics or ML theory, and advanced programming — none of which the candidate holds; their Python is analysis-level, not high-dimensional statistical inference. This is a deep-technical statistics research post far outside the candidate's field and skills.
jobs.salary: £43,277 to £51,714 pa (potential to £55,497), inclusive of London allowance

jobs.title: Engagement & Experience Officer
jobs.reason: This is an events / client-experience / engagement role whose essential criteria centre on managing executive-client relationships, planning event lifecycles with budgets and suppliers, and CRM systems — precisely the dedicated events/comms area where the candidate has limited experience, so paper fit is weak even though it is a broadly junior "Officer" post. It sits outside all three interest zones and offers no research or policy substance. Eligible on a technicality but a poor fit on nearly every axis.
jobs.salary: £36,513 to £41,565 (potential to £44,468) pa inclusive of London allowance

jobs.title: Employment Adviser - Southampton
jobs.reason: The role appears to be a frontline employment-advice / caseworker position, which does not match the candidate's research, policy and analytical profile — the skills fit is weak. It sits entirely outside all three interest zones, so it is barely worth surfacing despite being nominally eligible and entry-level.

jobs.title: Senior Administrator (Student Regulations)
jobs.reason: The role is degree-level administrative work and the candidate's HE-administration experience (Rectors' Conference, funding allocation) partly meets the "relevant HE administration in a student-facing environment" essential, though direct student-regulations/casework experience is thin. It sits well outside all three interest zones — this is university administration, not research or policy — so despite being in London and technically eligible, its priority is limited by weak paper alignment and low interest pull.
jobs.salary: £36,513–£41,565 pa (potential to £44,468) inclusive of London allowance

jobs.title: Head of International Customer Success
jobs.reason: This is a "Head of" senior leadership role requiring extensive experience building and managing multi-region CS organisations and managing managers — far beyond entry-level and disqualified on level. It is also a commercial customer-success function with no research or policy content, outside the candidate's skills and interest zones.

jobs.title: Video Producer
jobs.reason: The role's essential requirements — strong professional experience producing corporate video, filmmaking with Sony A7 and broadcast cameras, and expertise in Adobe Premiere Pro / After Effects — are specialist technical film-production skills the candidate does not possess. This is a dedicated video-production specialist post entirely outside the candidate's research/policy profile and interest zones.
jobs.salary: £43,277–£51,714 pa (progression to £55,497) inclusive of London allowance

jobs.title: Manager, Researcher Engagement
jobs.reason: The "Manager" title, combined with essential requirements for experience delivering digital events, running scalable engagement programmes, and developing playbooks and processes, places this beyond entry-level and outside the candidate's limited dedicated events/comms experience. It is also a specialist engagement/events role in academic publishing that sits outside the core interest zones.

jobs.title: Betriebsratsassistenz (m/w/d)
jobs.reason: This is an administrative assistant role supporting a works council — organisational, secretarial and coordination work that the candidate could technically perform, so it clears the eligibility gate. However, it sits entirely outside all three interest zones, has no research or policy content, and asks for assistance/administration experience in a personnel-relations context; it is a poor fit on nearly every axis.

jobs.title: Special Assistant
jobs.reason: This is a senior CEO-office role: the £63,790 salary and essential requirements for demonstrable experience managing senior government stakeholders, delivering advocacy strategies and briefing a CEO indicate several years of relevant post-graduation experience the candidate lacks. It functions as a de facto senior/experienced position, not an entry-level one, so it fails the level gate.
